item.text: {"facts":[{"source_id":"SRC-ba6415c76f67e70d","start_unit":7,"end_unit":8,"fact_summary":"EIGE's 2023–2024 administrative-data collection found that women constituted 80% of police-recorded intimate-partner-violence victims and 71% of domestic-violence victims in Germany, based on 2022 data; physical violence was the most commonly recorded form.","question_ids":["3B.7","3B.10"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"The finding uses 2022 administrative data collected in the 2023–2024 exercise, so it is a near-period structural context rather than a direct 2023 outcome attributable to Scholz.","ruler_attribution":"The source reports national administrative outcomes but does not attribute them to Olaf Scholz or identify a specific 2023 policy decision.","limitations":["Police-recorded cases do not measure all violence.","The data predates 2023.","No causal attribution to the federal government is provided."]},{"source_id":"SRC-ba6415c76f67e70d","start_unit":11,"end_unit":14,"fact_summary":"In 2022, police recorded 126,349 female intimate-partner-violence victims; women were 77% of physical intimate-partner-violence victims, 87% of psychological victims, 98% of sexual victims, and 99% of economic victims. EIGE noted that 2022 data are not comparable with earlier years because the offence selection was expanded, and survey data indicated psychological violence was substantially more prevalent than police records suggested.","question_ids":["3B.7","3B.10","6B.5"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"2022 data were presented in the 2023–2024 collection and provide pre-2023 context; the source does not establish a 2023 change.","ruler_attribution":"The figures describe German police and survey data; they do not establish a specific Scholz decision, implementation action, or responsibility.","limitations":["The 2022 series is not comparable with pre-2022 data because offence coverage expanded.","Police reporting likely understates psychological violence.","The figures count recorded victims and may include repeat victimization."]},{"source_id":"SRC-ba6415c76f67e70d","start_unit":17,"end_unit":19,"fact_summary":"Police recorded 171,076 female domestic-violence victims in Germany in 2022. Women represented 69% of physical domestic-violence victims, 76% of psychological victims, 88% of sexual victims, and 97% of economic victims; the corresponding female counts were 117,900, 45,648, 7,421, and 107.","question_ids":["3B.6","3B.7","3B.10"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"These are 2022 administrative figures reported through the 2023–2024 collection, not direct 2023 measurements.","ruler_attribution":"The source reports police-recorded national outcomes without linking them to Scholz's formal actions or federal implementation choices.","limitations":["The categories are aggregated from national offences and do not correspond exactly to ICCS categories.","The figures measure police-recorded victims, not total prevalence.","Domestic-violence data include intimate-partner violence."]},{"source_id":"SRC-ba6415c76f67e70d","start_unit":22,"end_unit":25,"fact_summary":"In 2022, women constituted 87% of intimate-partner homicide victims (137 of 158) and 73% of domestic-homicide victims (198 of 271); police also recorded 2,808 female intimate-partner rape victims and 3,063 female domestic-rape victims.","question_ids":["3B.6","3B.7","3B.10"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"The figures cover 2022 and therefore function as near-period context for 2023 rather than direct 2023 evidence.","ruler_attribution":"The source presents police-recorded homicide and rape outcomes and does not attribute them to Scholz or a particular government measure.","limitations":["The source does not provide 2023 figures.","Homicide data cover intentional homicide and exclude non-intentional homicide.","Police-recorded victim counts may not capture unreported offences."]},{"source_id":"SRC-ba6415c76f67e70d","start_unit":27,"end_unit":28,"fact_summary":"In 2020, German family courts granted 2,591 protection orders to women victims of violence and stalking, representing 84% of all granted protection orders (2,591 of 3,065).","question_ids":["3B.4","3B.7"],"polarity":"favorable","period_fit":"This is 2020 data, substantially preceding the 2023 target period, and is historical institutional context only.","ruler_attribution":"The finding concerns family-court activity under the Violence Protection Act; it does not identify a Scholz-era decision or 2023 implementation.","limitations":["No 2023 protection-order figure is supplied.","The data cover violence in any relationship, not only intimate or domestic violence.","The source does not assess order effectiveness or enforcement."]},{"source_id":"SRC-ba6415c76f67e70d","start_unit":30,"end_unit":31,"fact_summary":"EIGE reported that Germany had widely available police data on victims and reported perpetrators, but justice-sector data were limited: data were retrieved only for 2020 protection orders, and no data were available on perpetrators prosecuted, sentenced, or imprisoned.","question_ids":["3B.4","3B.5","3B.7","3B.10","6B.5"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"This institutional finding was made in the 2023–2024 collection and is relevant to the 2023 period, although it describes data-system coverage rather than a dated 2023 outcome.","ruler_attribution":"The source identifies a national justice-data limitation but does not attribute its existence or correction to Scholz.","limitations":["The finding concerns availability of administrative data, not necessarily absence of prosecutions or imprisonment.","It does not identify the responsible institution or any reform decision.","It does not establish whether the limitation was corrected during 2023."]}],"documents_with_no_material_fact":[],"batch_limitations":["The document primarily reports German violence indicators for 2022, with some protection-order data from 2020; it provides little direct evidence about Olaf Scholz's specific 2023 decisions, policies, appointments, budgets, or implementation.","No material facts were found for chapters 1B, 2B, 4B, 5B, 7B, or 8B."]}
